citation.title: Estimation of edge electron temperature profiles via forward modelling of the electron cyclotron radiation transport at ASDEX Upgrade
citation.authors: S K Rathgeber, L Barrera, T Eich, R Fischer, B Nold, W Suttrop, M Willensdorfer, E Wolfrum and the ASDEX Upgrade Team

topic: Offline Bayesian forward modelling of ECE radiation transport for edge electron Te in ASDEX Upgrade H-modes.
own_question: How can reliable edge electron Te profiles be obtained from optically thin and steep-gradient ECE data, including the shine-through peak?
actual_method_and_evidence: ECE radiation-transport forward model inside integrated data analysis with lithium-beam and interferometer density. Shown on a few discharges, sensitivity scans, one synthetic reconstruction, and Thomson and Langmuir comparisons with profile shifts. Each forward evaluation takes about 0.13 s, and a full run per time point takes about 10 min.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Near steep H-mode edges, ECE radiation temperature can differ from local electron Te, so treating it as the local temperature can mislead; forward modelling has been used to address this offline.
claim_checks.qualification: Electron ECE only, ASDEX Upgrade; offline analysis. Not about impurity CES, ion temperature, or KSTAR.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Offline time-window profile fits. There is no causal nowcasting and no report-arrival analysis.
validation_if_relevant: Validation is case studies, not held-out statistical validation.
forbidden_inferences: Not evidence about the reliability of CES impurity Ti labels.
Not evidence that ECEI voltages carry information about ion temperature.
The 0.13 s and 10 min timings do not bear on our 10 ms budget.
Does not show that all prior work was noncausal or limited to electrons.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional citation only, if the paper explains why raw ECE-type signals are not calibrated local Te. Its diagnostic, quantity and machine differ from our work.
